title: United States off the mark at T20 World Cup to keep Super Eight hopes alive
content:
The United States have achieved their first victory at this year’s T20 World Cup by thrashing the Netherlands by an impressive 93 runs to keep their hopes of reaching the Super Eight phase alive.

India-born Harmeet Singh took 4-21 off his four overs, the best figures ever recorded for the U.S. at the tournament, to bamboozle the Dutch under the lights in Chennai as, in reply to 196-6, they were dismissed for only 103.

The Netherlands lost their last five wickets for 28 runs with veteran seamer Shadley van Schalkwyk, one of the stars of the tournament in India and Sri Lanka to date, mopping up the tail to claim another three wickets.

That took his tally to 11 in three matches, strengthening his position as the leading wicket taker at the finals to date. He is four clear of Zimbabwe’s Blessing Muzarabani, Lungi Ngidi of South Africa and team-mate Harmeet.

The victory sees the U.S. leapfrog their opponents to go third in Group A. Their chances of reaching the Super Eight stage of the tournament, and emulating their eye-catching achievement from 2024, will hinge upon recording another emphatic win from their final group match, against the section’s bottom-placed side, Namibia, and hoping other results go their way.

“We keep trusting, we keep fighting,” said Harmeet after being given his player-of-the-match award. “Our first two games were also close ones, and we put up a lot of competition. We’ve shown the world what we can do and, today, we showed what we can do with the ball as well.”

The U.S., beaten by India and Pakistan in their first two games, batted impressively at the Chepauk Stadium.

Openers Shayan Jahangir (20) and Monank Patel (36) set the tone before Saiteja Mukkamalla, of Plainsboro, New Jersey, composed a fine 79 off 51 balls. The 21-year-old held the innings together, with Shubham Ranjane injecting some late momentum by smashing 48 not out off 24 deliveries.

“He’s an incredible talent for the USA,” captain Patel told the post-match presentation when asked about Mukkamalla’s contribution to the win. “The way he’s been batting for the last two years… it’s as if he’s been playing for 10 years. He’s a very mature player. He took the responsibility because we wanted one of the top three to bat long.

“I’m really happy with the way we played today. Winning the toss and batting first wasn’t easy, but we showed the intent we’d been missing in our first two games. We came back really well in the batting department. The top order took the responsibility and played with intent and scored really well.

“We learned a lot from our first two games, and we’re showing that now.”

The U.S. made history two years ago by qualifying for the Super Eight stage of the tournament — they were co-hosts along with the West Indies — after beating Canada and, most notably, Pakistan in the group stage. That was their first appearance at the T20 World Cup.

India will take on Pakistan in the most eagerly anticipated fixture of the tournament in Colombo on Sunday after Pakistan’s government ended its initial order for a boycott.
